name: Arun Ayduğan
bio:
Arun Ayduğan is a director, screenwriter, actor, theatre director, and visual artist born on 13 July 2010 in Çanakkale, Türkiye. Without formal academic training in cinema or the performing arts, he has developed his artistic practice independently.

His involvement in the arts began in childhood with theatre. At the age of ten, he took part in his school's English drama activities, gaining his first stage experience. His interest in filmmaking developed through stop-motion experiments, eventually leading him to write and direct his own films.

Directing and screenwriting occupy a central place in Ayduğan's cinematic practice. Completed in 2025, The Mind Trilogy is a project exploring the three-stage writing process of a writer. The film has been selected for Lift-Off First-Time Filmmaker Sessions and the FilmRoads International Student Film Festival.

His 2026 film Fallen From Olympus, developed over two and a half years, was filmed entirely in Homeric Greek, without the use of any modern language. Set in the aftermath of the Trojan War, the film follows a soldier confronting death and explores the futility of war and the human condition in the face of mortality.

The film received an Honourable Mention at the Athens International Monthly Art Film Festival and had its world premiere at the INNOVART Film Festival, where it received five nominations. It was also selected for various programmes of the Lift-Off Global Network and the Four River Film Festival, where it won Best International Free Style Film. Ayduğan received the Best New Director award at the Athens Marathon International Film Festival. The film was named a semi-finalist at the Altavilla Film Festival and a finalist at the 11th Kısa'dan Hisse Film Festival, where it was nominated for Best Student Film. Its Turkish premiere took place on 4 September 2026 at the Troy Museum in Çanakkale, Türkiye.

Among Ayduğan's screenwriting projects is Red Petals, based on the real wartime experiences of his great-great-grandfather in Germany during the Second World War. The screenplay reached the semi-finalist stage at the Scriptmatix Student Filmmakers Showcase.

In theatre, Ayduğan wrote, directed, and performed the one-person play Mozart da Çocuktu. He also portrayed William Shakespeare in his play Waiting for Hamlet. In 2026, he undertook the direction of Anton Chekhov's The Bear and The Celebration.

Ayduğan also works in photography and digital surrealist illustration. In 2026, he digitally published MON JeVu, his first personal exhibition, consisting of surrealist digital illustrations created over his own photographs.

His latest film project, The Last Days of Napoléon, is a medium-length historical drama focusing on Napoleon Bonaparte's final period in exile on Saint Helena. Seeking to present an unconventional portrait of Napoleon in cinema, the film is scheduled to reach audiences in 2028.

credits.title: The Anatomy of a Dad Joke: Or the World's Most Underrated Art
credits.overview: By observing his own family over an extended period, conducting covert recordings and interviews, Arun Ayduğan has completed The Anatomy of a Dad Joke, a documentary that teaches us far more than we could ever have expected.

credits.title: The Last Days of Napoléon
credits.overview: Exiled to the remote island of Saint Helena, Napoleon Bonaparte spends his final days accompanied by a small circle of attendants. As he wanders the island and goes about his daily routines, fragments of his past resurface in unexpected moments.

credits.title: Fallen From Olympus
credits.overview: Following the Trojan War, a soldier facing death encounters Thanatos and is drawn into a mythological confrontation about life, fate, and the meaninglessness of war.

credits.title: A Few of Shakespeare's Days of Despair
credits.overview: Unable to write for a long time, William Shakespeare embarks on a desperate search for inspiration. But everything he encounters forces him to confront his own legacy and creative burnout.

credits.title: The Mind Trilogy
credits.overview: A writer confronts his own mind through a journey of observation, listening, and writing.
